claim.quote: The resulting primary energy spectra show that the knee in the all particle spectrum is due to a steepening of the spectra of light elements

date.note: arXiv v1 date; published in Astropart. Phys. 24, 1 (2005).

name: The knee is due to a steepening of the light-element spectra

official_url.quote: KASCADE measurements of energy spectra for elemental groups of cosmic rays: Results and open problems

summary.plain: By unfolding the electron and muon numbers of air showers, KASCADE separated cosmic rays into groups of elements. It found the "knee" in the overall spectrum comes from light elements running out, while noting that neither hadronic-interaction model fitted all the data.
summary.technical: Two-dimensional unfolding of the electron-muon number spectrum with QGSJet and SIBYLL simulations gives energy spectra of elemental groups; the all-particle knee is due to a steepening of the light-element spectra, and neither simulation set describes the data consistently over the whole energy range.

title: KASCADE measurements of energy spectra for elemental groups of cosmic rays: Results and open problems
why_it_matters: The abstract says the knee in the all-particle spectrum is due to a steepening of the light-element spectra, and also that neither of the two hadronic-interaction simulation sets describes the data consistently.
